subject: Secure export safeguards and subprocessor key-splitting — HealthGrid follow-up
messages:
From: Alan Ruiz <alan.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Privacy Ops <privacy@healthgrid.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Export safeguards - HealthGrid PII export request

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our privacy team is running a quick review ahead of an initial export of de-identified customer records into Redwood for a short-term ML eval. They asked for a plain description of the safeguards around:

- Pseudonymization steps applied before export
- Key custody model (who holds keys, split-key options)
- Cross-border routing rules and any fail-open behaviors
- Evidence/artifacts we can provide for our SOC2/QoS checks (export logs, integrity proofs)

Two immediate asks: can you confirm whether Redwood supports a split-key arrangement (HealthGrid holds a KMS key share; Redwood holds an envelope key), and whether we can get a dataflow diagram showing where tokenization/pseudonymization happens?

If useful, I can share the specific SSQ sections that triggered these asks. Appreciate a short write-up or playbook we can attach to our intake.

Thanks,
Alan
Privacy Lead, HealthGrid
attachments: none

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Ruiz <alan.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export safeguards - HealthGrid PII export request

Alan —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, followed by proposed next steps and artifacts.

1) Split-key support: Yes. Redwood can implement an envelope encryption flow where HealthGrid provides a KMS-managed key share (via your KMS or a customer-managed HSM) that wraps the per-export CEK (content encryption key). Redwood retains an ephemeral envelope key that is also required for decryption; both pieces are needed to unwrap. This achieves split custody for exports.

2) Pseudonymization location: We support two modes:
   - Pre-export pseudonymization (recommended for regulated datasets): HealthGrid runs the tokenization step in your environment before transfer (we document a small client tool to canonicalize identifiers).
   - Redwood-side pseudonymization: For convenience we can tokenize on ingest inside a private VPC deployment, using an HSM-backed key. When used, we store only mapping digests in an encrypted store; original identifiers are never persisted in plaintext.

3) Cross-border routing and fail-open: By default routing follows the routing policy in the DPA annex (region = onboarding region). We do not perform automatic fail-open to another region for exports containing PII; in the event of a capacity failure we will return a 503 and surface the fallback model variant, but export operations that require export of identifiers are blocked unless explicitly allowed in contract.

Artifacts we can provide: export-playbook (step-by-step), signed export manifest (SHA256), per-export audit log (immutable), and an access matrix slice showing which roles can request exports.

I attached a short export safeguards playbook and a draft dataflow SVG that maps pseudonymization and KMS handoff points. Can you confirm if HealthGrid requires the pre-export tokenization mode only, or if you want Redwood-side tokenization with customer KMS?

Next steps:
- HealthGrid to confirm preferred pseudonymization mode and regulatory region(s)
- Redwood to provide a DPA annex draft with the split-key clause and a proposed DocuSign workflow
- We set up a short call with Privacy Ops if there are follow-up technical questions

Attachments: redwood-export-safeguards-v1.pdf (5 pages) — playbook, healthgrid-dataflow-diagram.svg

Best,
Jonas Weber
Manager, Security & Privacy — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0179

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Ruiz <alan.ruiz@healthgrid.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export safeguards - HealthGrid PII export request

Alan / team —

Following up with concrete asks from our side so we can fast-track the DPA annex and the DocuSign handoff. Proposed action items:

- HealthGrid to confirm mode: "pre-export tokenization" OR "Redwood-tokenize with customer KMS". If pre-export, share the tokenization CLI version you plan to use and a small sample manifest (no PII inside).
- If you choose Redwood-side tokenization we will require a KMS policy document and enable key-split. Please also confirm whether HealthGrid wants the KMS in us-central1 or eu-west1 (affects routing).
- Privacy Ops: we will draft a limited export clause (see attached dpa-annex-draft.docx) that enumerates the allowed recipients and retention window. Please flag any non-standard asks.
- Required artifacts for your compliance team: pseudonymization runbook, export audit manifest, audit logs (retention: 2 years default, can be extended), and the SVG dataflow.

I'll set a 30-min sync for Thursday to walk through the diagram and the DocuSign flow. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 1) confirm mode & region, 2) signatory list for DocuSign, 3) timeline for a sandbox export.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
attachments: dpa-annex-draft.docx

From: Alan Ruiz <alan.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Privacy Ops <privacy@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export safeguards - HealthGrid PII export request

Marissa / Jonas —

Appreciate the thorough write-up and the artifacts. We are leaning toward pre-export tokenization for the first run to keep the blast radius minimal.

Next steps on our end:
- I will route the playbook and diagram to our Privacy Ops and confirm the tokenization CLI version by EOD Friday.
- I also confirmed we prefer us-central1 for the KMS if we ever use Redwood-side tokenization.

We'll be in touch after Privacy Ops reviews the draft annex — likely some small edits to the retention window. For now please go ahead and schedule the Thurs call and include a short slot for DocuSign workflow review.

Thanks,
Alan
Privacy Lead, HealthGrid
